A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecAF research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation evaluations, component ablations, model-scaling experiments, and qualitative analyses in Tables 1–8 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds native-grounding comparisons, prompt ablations, subset evaluation, and qualitative experiments in its appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same vision-aware rollout, contrastive and complementary fusion, point generation, and SAM2 tracklet scoring. The original prompts also remain unchanged. Appendix prompt variants are experimental ablations, while negative-point prompting is suggested only as future work.

E1.justification: The five benchmark datasets remain unchanged. Appendix I adds targeted qualitative evaluation of part-level expressions, contrasting whole-person localization with shirt, face, and glasses targets. The ReasonVOS subset analysis uses retained benchmark data rather than adding a dataset.

E2.justification: Appendix E/Table 9 introduces four evaluated native Qwen2.5-VL grounding baselines combined with SAM2. Table 2 also adds VRS-HQ to the ReasonVOS comparison, where v1 reported no result for it. These substantially expand the comparison beyond the retained attention-based and trained methods.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce frame-wise segmentation, first-frame propagation, reference/key-frame grounding, and matched 16-frame grounding protocols. Appendix F varies the three prompt types, and Appendix H evaluates a specified 187-of-458 ReasonVOS subset. These extend the evaluation design; the original metrics and default thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds three variants for each of the three prompt types, testing wording and information dependence in Tables 10–12. It also adds quantitative and qualitative similar-object discrimination analyses, part-level failure analysis, and additional implicit-expression case studies. The earlier component ablations and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. SAM confidence and attention-consistency scores are algorithmic quantities, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 revise many benchmark and ablation values. For Qwen2.5-VL-7B DecAF, reported J&F changes from 59.7 to 63.9 on ReasonVOS, 50.3 to 54.2 on ReVOS overall, and 43.5 to 48.1 on MeViS. Tables 9–13 add grounding, prompt, and subset results. The PDFs do not explain the causes of the existing-score revisions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–8 are retained, including rollout accumulation, vision-aware weighting, point selection, and attention-consistency scoring. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the central training-free fusion and segmentation contributions. The conclusion newly claims superiority over training-based methods on ReasonVOS and proposes applicability beyond vision through modality-agnostic attention fusion. These extend the performance claim and outlook without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: New appendices interpret native-grounding weaknesses, prompt sensitivity, and resilience to similar-object distractors. Appendix I adds a substantive limitation: correctly localized parts can still produce whole-object SAM2 masks because a positive point does not unambiguously specify segmentation granularity. Earlier failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies alternative prompt templates, native-grounding setup details, and LLaVA-OV Loc-Head adaptation instructions concerning tiling and attention-sink exclusion. It also changes the code-release statement from future availability to stated availability. The core implementation defaults remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Section 2 are unchanged. The introduction more explicitly positions DecAF against joint MLLM–segmentation training costs and generalization limitations, while the new appendices extend its positioning against native Qwen grounding and Loc-Head across backbones.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction and conclusion, expands the main qualitative discussion, updates the publication header, and adds Appendices E–J. The existing section order, methodology exposition, and related-work narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–13 and substantially expands visual analysis through Figures 10–20, including query points, ground truth, competing masks, and part-level targets. v1 Figures 5–6 are combined and moved into the main text as v2 Figure 4; the other earlier qualitative examples are retained under revised numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through matched native-grounding controls, systematic prompt ablations, and similar-object subset comparisons in Tables 9–13. Its part-level analysis also clarifies a meaningful SAM2 limitation. Unexplained revisions to existing scores and absent uncertainty estimates remain weaknesses, but the stronger controls and clearer applicability boundaries substantially improve the paper beyond merely reporting higher performance.
